paper.title: Graph-based interactive bibliographic information retrieval systems

evidence.paraphrase: The work develops interactive graph-based systems for retrieving papers and other bibliographic entities with complex queries.
Its evaluations concern query-processing time, query representation, and usability rather than search recall, sensitivity, retrieval ceilings, or reachable relevant records.

reviews.rationale: The paper is within scholarly bibliographic retrieval, but the reported contribution and evaluation do not validate search reachability or recall against a relevant-record benchmark. The abstract is sufficient to exclude it from this evidence role.

paper.title: How to Write Effective Prompts for Screening Biomedical Literature Using Large Language Models

evidence.paraphrase: The paper addresses LLM-assisted abstract screening within systematic reviews and retains expert oversight as part of that evidence-selection workflow.
Recall and precision are used to evaluate inclusion screening under different prompts, not the completeness, sensitivity, ceiling, or reachability of literature retrieval.

reviews.rationale: This is an in-scope evidence-selection workflow, but its evaluated outcome is screening classification rather than validation of the preceding literature search or candidate-pool reachability. It therefore does not support the assigned evidence role.

paper.title: Diagnosis of Cervical Cancer and Pre-Cancerous Lesions by Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review

evidence.paraphrase: The review evaluates AI systems for clinical prediction, screening, and diagnosis of cervical cancer and precancerous lesions.
The reported sensitivity and specificity refer to diagnostic detection of cervical lesions, not validation or recall of the literature search.

reviews.rationale: The paper is a clinical diagnostic-performance review rather than a study of scholarly retrieval or evidence-selection methods. Its use of search and sensitivity terminology is not evidence for literature-search reachability.

paper.title: The emergence of large language models as tools in literature reviews: a large language model-assisted systematic review

evidence.paraphrase: The review surveys LLM use across scientific-review workflows, including projects concerned with searching for publications.
The quantitative performance comparison reported in the abstract concerns data extraction, while searching is described only as a category count without search-validation outcomes.

reviews.rationale: The review is relevant to automated literature-review workflows, but the abstract does not provide a method or result for validating search recall, sensitivity, retrieval ceilings, or reachable records. Mentioning search automation at category level is too generic to fill the assigned role.

paper.title: ADVANCED COMPUTING APPLICATIONS IN BI DASHBOARDS: IMPROVING REAL-TIME DECISION SUPPORT FOR GLOBAL ENTERPRISES

evidence.paraphrase: The review synthesizes computing architectures, latency, freshness, governance, and reliability for enterprise business-intelligence dashboards.
Its sensitivity analyses address heterogeneity in dashboard-technology evidence, not the validation, recall, or reachability of a scholarly literature search.

reviews.rationale: The contribution concerns enterprise BI dashboard infrastructure and performance, outside scholarly search and evidence-selection workflows. Systematic-review and sensitivity language does not make it relevant to literature-search validation.
